item.title: Deep Unrolling of Lanczos-based Laplacian Eigensolver for Crop Classification in Satellite Images
item.description: arXiv:2611.14709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Per-pixel crop classification in satellite images is an important pre-processing step in remote crop monitoring. Leveraging progress in signed graph signal processing, we build an interpretable and lightweight neural network for binary crop classification (e.g., corn versus non-corn) in two stages: i) learn a signed graph from data, and ii) unroll a Lanczos-based eigensolver to compute the eigenvector $\u_1$ associated with the smallest eigenvalue of a hybrid graph Laplacian $\cL$ for spectral clustering. Specifically, we first construct a near-balanced signed graph $\cG^s$, where signed edge weights $w_{i,j}\in(-1,1)$ are computed from learned feature distances $d_{i,j}$ via a hyperbolic tangent mapping. Given $\cG^s$, we estimate $\u_1$ by unrolling the Lanczos algorithm and use $\mathrm{sign}(\u_1)$ for binary classification. Mathematically, we develop a theorem establishing conditions under which $\u_1$ can be well approximated after finite Lanczos iterations. Motivated by this theorem, we relax the classical Lanczos orthogonality constraints during unrolling and optimize end-to-end classification performance while promoting the derived conditions for accurate eigenvector approximation. Experiments on real-world Harmonized Landsat-Sentinel imagery show classification performance comparable to state-of-the-art deep learning models while reducing parameters by up to two orders of magnitude.
item.dc:creator: Parham Eftekhar, Gene Cheung

item.title: Joint Beamforming and Duplex-Mode Segment Selection for Secure Uplink Transmission in Pinching Antenna Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.14712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pinching antenna systems (PASS) have recently emerged as a promising architecture for reconfigurable, flexible and proximity-driven signal delivery. In this paper, we propose a segmented waveguide-based PASS architecture for enabling secure uplink communications, where each segment activates at most one pinching antenna (PA), which inherently eliminates the inter-antenna re-radiation effect and yields a tractable uplink signal model. To protect the uplink transmission against eavesdropping, the base station (BS) injects artificial noise (AN) toward the eavesdroppers via selected downlink segments using a duplex-mode segment selection mechanism, which dynamically configures each segment for either uplink reception or downlink AN transmission through switch-controlled fiber connections. We formulate the secrecy energy efficiency (SEE) maximization problem as a mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) that jointly optimizes the receive beamforming vector, AN covariance, user transmit power, pinching antenna positions, and duplex-mode segment assignment. Given the non-convex and combinatorial nature of the problem, we develop an efficient alternating optimization (AO) framework, where the resulting subproblems are solved using the Dinkelbach method combined with successive convex approximation (SCA) and penalty-based relaxation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms benchmark schemes in terms of SEE and robustness against waveguide attenuation. Moreover, AN effectively suppresses information leakage, while PA mobility, duplex-mode segment allocation, and waveguide segmentation further improve secrecy performance through flexible positioning and reduced in-waveguide propagation loss.

item.title: Performance Analysis of Quantization-Aware Neural Channel Estimation with Low-Precision Inference
item.description: arXiv:2611.14757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural channel estimators can improve radio performance of 5G receivers, but real-time deployment in the radio access network (RAN) imposes strict latency and power budgets. Prior studies of quantized neural channel estimators assess this cost through mean-squared error or analytic operation counts. In this paper, we train a 1D convolutional neural network (CNN) channel estimator for the 5G NR physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) with INT8 and FP8 quantization-aware training (QAT), and we evaluate its radio performance together with its latency, power, and energy on an NVIDIA H100 GPU. On TDL-A and TDL-C channels at user equipment (UE) speeds up to 35 m/s, both 8-bit models stay within 0.025 dB of FP32 at 10% block error rate (BLER). At batch size 128, INT8 reduces the latency by 16%, the incremental GPU power by 33%, and the energy per query by 26%, compared with 6%, 26%, and 21% for FP8. INT8 is therefore the preferred format.
item.dc:creator: Joonas T\"orm\"al\"a, SaiKrishna Saketh Yellapragada, Eeli Susan, Esa Ollila

item.title: Full-Duplex Communication for Pinching Antenna Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.14882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates multiuser full-duplex (FD) communication assisted by a multiwaveguide pinching-antenna system (PASS) where each dielectric waveguide can be dynamically configured to operate in either downlink transmission or uplink reception mode. We develop a channel model that accounts for in-waveguide power attenuation and cumulative pinching antenna (PA)-induced phase shift. Building on this model, we jointly optimize the waveguide modes, PA locations, PA radiation/collection coefficients, downlink beamformers, uplink receive combiners, and uplink transmit powers to maximize the downlink weighted sum-rate (WSR) subject to uplink quality-of-service (QoS) requirements and power constraints. To tackle the resulting mixed-integer nonconvex resource allocation problem, we propose a low-complexity hierarchical block coordinate descent algorithm that capitalizes on weighted minimum mean-square error, fractional programming, majorization-minimization, and the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) to obtain a high-quality suboptimal solution. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed FD-PASS outperforms an FD base station equipped with fixed antennas and exhibits greater robustness against residual self-interference. Moreover, ignoring cumulative PA-induced phase shifts can produce QoS-infeasible designs.
item.dc:creator: Shaokang Hu, Ruotong Zhao, Derrick Wing Kwan Ng, Jinhong Yuan

item.title: Affine Frequency Division Multiplexing With Pre-Chirp Spreading Index Modulation: A CSI-Driven Secure Transmission Framework
item.description: arXiv:2611.15045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The flexible configurability of pre-chirp parameters in affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) provides new degrees of freedom for designing covert communication mechanisms. Leveraging this property, this paper proposes a covert AFDM pre-chirp spreading index modulation (IM) framework referred to as AFDM-PCS-IM, tailored for high-mobility scenarios. Specifically, an orthogonal pre-chirp parameter codebook is constructed by exploiting the tunability of the pre-chirp parameters. To enhance covertness, the legitimate channel state information (CSI) is utilized to generate controlled perturbations that encrypt the codebook, thereby tightly coupling the modulation structure with instantaneous channel characteristics. The encrypted pre-chirp codebook is then employed as an IM dimension for information transmission, where the index bits are conveyed through the selection of pre-chirp parameter sequences. Since eavesdroppers cannot obtain consistent CSI, they are unable to reconstruct the encrypted codebook and thus cannot reliably recover any useful information. Moreover, to address channel estimation errors inherent in practical communication environments, a noise-aware CSI quantizer is further introduced to improve robustness under imperfect CSI conditions. Finally, a low-complexity two-layer message passing detector with Walsh code constraints (TLMP-WC) is developed to enable efficient large-scale data detection while simultaneously enhancing the detection reliability. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed AFDM-PCS-IM framework with the TLMP-WC detector achieves superior covertness, improved bit error rate (BER) performance, and reduced computational complexity compared with the state-of-the-art schemes.
item.dc:creator: Yiwei Tao, Miaowen Wen, Yao Ge, Merouane Debbah, Erdal Panayirci

item.title: Multi-Band Indoor MIMO Channel Measurements Across Sub-6 GHz, Mid-Band and mmWave: Comparing 2.55 GHz, 12.75 GHz and 25.5 GHz
item.description: arXiv:2611.15285v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Future wireless systems for indoor applications are expected to extend their operating frequencies from sub-6 GHz to mid-band and millimeter wave (mmWave) frequencies to support higher data rates. To characterize the frequency-dependent propagation behavior across these bands, multi-band channel measurements are essential. In this work, we conduct double-directional multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channel measurements in an indoor environment to enable a consistent comparison across three frequency bands. Measurements are performed using a 16x16 MIMO configuration at center frequencies of 2.55 GHz, 12.75 GHz and 25.5 GHz, covering both line-of-sight (LOS) and obstructed line-of-sight (OLOS) conditions. The measured channels are processed using the space-alternating generalized expectation maximization (SAGE) algorithm to extract multipath parameters, which are subsequently used to characterize the angular power distributions across the three frequency bands. The results show substantial angular-domain similarity across all three bands in both LOS and OLOS conditions, while also highlighting frequency-dependent variations.

item.title: Multi-Label Classification with Constrained Search for Inverse Design of a 16x16 Reconfigurable Pixel Antenna
item.description: arXiv:2611.15286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, an inverse design method is presented for a 16x16 reconfigurable pixel antenna with 480 binary switches, giving 2480 possible patterns, far beyond what full-wave simulation can explore. Given a target frequency between 1 and 6 GHz, the method searches for a switch configuration whose simulated resonance lies close to the target. A forward surrogate model is trained on 22,152 full- wave simulated patterns to predict where a given switch pattern resonates. The forward task is formulated as multi-label classification over 100 frequency bins rather than reflection-coefficient regression, because a curve-fitting objective is dominated by the flat baseline around the narrow resonances of this structure. The inverse design is a simulated annealing search over the switch state, with a connectivity constraint maintained at every step so that every pattern generated is a valid antenna. The proposed methodology combines resonance-focused surrogate modelling with connectivity-constrained discrete optimization, enabling candidate generation without full-wave solver calls during the search. The pipeline is verified in CST Microwave Studio by simulating 220 predicted candidates, ten for each of 22 target frequencies. For each request, the best of the ten candidates reached a median frequency error of 23 MHz across the 22 targets, compared with 35 MHz for a solver-guided search using 200 simulations for each target. The proposed methodology therefore enables automatic switch configuration to achieve a requested resonant frequency, eliminating solver calls during the search and manual redesign of the antenna geometry.
item.dc:creator: Nadeem Rather, Holger Claussen, Lester Ho

item.title: Analytical Characterization of Radial Resolution at Oblique Angles for Near-Field Communications
item.description: arXiv:2611.15326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Exploiting radial resolvability in near-field communications requires analytical expressions that directly map physical beam parameters to resolution-controllable focal regions. However, beam characterization at oblique angles produces complex algebraic expressions that mask these critical interactions. In this work, we introduce an electromagnetic-aware analytical model built upon a tight upper bound of the spatial power density. This approach yields compact, closed-form solutions for the peak intensity position and radial focal extent, enabling the design of contiguous multi-user focal regions with controlled radial resolution. Performance evaluations confirm that the framework closely tracks exact solutions while facilitating system dimensioning and inter-beam interference management across varying steering angles.
item.dc:creator: Viviana Centritto, Sotiris Droulias, Angeliki Alexiou

item.title: Deep Learning-Assisted Optimization of Large Domino-Tiled Phased Arrays for Dual-Band LEO Satellite Communications
item.description: arXiv:2611.15390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Irregular domino tiling reduces the number of transmit/receive modules (TRMs) of large phased arrays, but its design requires repeated pattern evaluations whose cost grows rapidly with aperture size. This paper presents a hybrid deep learning and optimization framework for large domino-tiled arrays. A local-flip Markov chain generator, about $5.2\times$ faster than a randomized greedy baseline, produces balanced tilings with nearly equal numbers of horizontal and vertical dominoes, and a Tabu Search engine reaches a sidelobe level (SLL) about $0.8$~dB lower than a genetic algorithm, simulated annealing, and iterated local search at comparable directivity. These tools build the dataset on which a convolutional neural network (CNN) surrogate is trained to predict, from the tiling structure alone, whether a candidate yields a favorable multi-angle SLL. Gating the Tabu Search with the surrogate removes $60.6$--$70.6\%$ of the full evaluations and speeds up the search by $2.56$--$3.80$ times for apertures from $20\times20$ to $100\times100$ elements, without degrading the solution quality. A convex amplitude--phase optimization of the fixed tilings then gives equal or higher directivity than two state-of-the-art methods at a comparable SLL, with more than an order of magnitude shorter computation time. Finally, the framework is applied to a $36\times36$ dual-band circularly polarized array for low Earth orbit (LEO) terminals at $11.2$ and $14.0$~GHz, whose bands are a factor of $1.25$ apart, using $648$ dominoes and a common element spacing selected from a sweep. The array scans to $50^\circ$ with no grating lobe and, compared with a reference irregular array, gives higher directivity over most of the scan range, a lower SLL at large scan angles, and a spacing that is more practical for the lower band.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Mashayekhi, Gholamreza Askari

item.title: Geometry-based Efficient Airy Beam Training for Quasi-LoS in Terahertz Near-field Communications
item.description: arXiv:2611.15497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With enlarged antenna apertures in Terahertz (THz) communications, near-field propagation becomes increasingly dominant, highlighting quasi-line-of-sight (quasi-LoS) scenarios with partial blockage. Airy beams offer a promising solution through their curved trajectories, but existing training methods for unknown blockage rely on computationally intensive parameter searches or learning-based approaches. In this paper, we propose an efficient geometry-based Airy beam training framework for uniform linear array (ULA) and uniform planar array (UPA) systems. First, theoretical feasibility bounds under finite apertures are derived to eliminate infeasible codewords. A performance-oriented Slope-Depth Geometric Codebook (SDGC) is then developed using bending-direction probing and geometric sampling. To further reduce training overhead, a latency-oriented Bijective 1D Geometric Codebook (B1GC) is proposed by mapping blockage-avoidance waypoints to receiver targets, enabling one-dimensional search. For UPA systems, a hybrid focusing--Airy mode is introduced, using four probe beams to identify the blockage-avoidance dimension and bending direction, followed by Airy beam training and orthogonal near-field focusing. Simulations show that SDGC achieves 14.8 bit/s/Hz average spectral efficiency with 40.9\% lower training overhead than the hierarchical focusing--Airy codebook (HFAC), while B1GC reduces overhead by 87.1\% with comparable performance. The UPA results further demonstrate effectiveness under two-dimensional blockage.
item.dc:creator: Wenqi Zhao, Chong Han

item.title: A Tutorial on Infrastructure Self-Calibration for Radio-Based Indoor Positioning
item.description: arXiv:2611.15503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Radio positioning needs the positions of its anchors, access points, base stations, or reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, and manual surveying is costly and error-prone. Calibrating this infrastructure from its own measurements is one estimation problem, studied in at least four communities as self-calibration, auto-positioning, anchor self-localization, network localization, or radio simultaneous localization and mapping. This tutorial teaches the problem through one factor graph. The measurement topology sets its factors, the reference information enters as priors, and other measurement models add nuisance states. The tutorial shows what ranges can identify, from rigidity to the motion a mobile device must contribute, and presents multidimensional scaling, nonlinear least squares, recursive filters, and convex relaxations as inference engines over this graph. One session of a ten-anchor ultra-wideband deployment is carried through every step, and recordings from a second, harsher deployment and a public partial mesh serve as contrasts. The examples illustrate three lessons. On a full mesh, choose a robust loss and set its scale first, and calibrate with the engine of the positioning system, since the engines then reach similar errors. On thinned or partial meshes, test the result at surveyed check points, because the start decides which minimum a solver reaches. On a line-of-sight deployment, estimate range offsets, which lower the error floor that a systematic ranging bias sets and a robust loss cannot remove. A decision tree and a table of their effects turn them into deployment guidance. Code and result tables are openly released, and the data are published separately.
item.dc:creator: Paul Schwarzbach

item.title: Over-the-Air Computation for Imperfectly Synchronized Multi-View Semantic Communication
item.description: arXiv:2611.15520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compared to classical task-agnostic communication systems, which focus on reliable transmission of a message, semantic communication (SemCom) focuses on transmitting the task-relevant meaning behind the message. In this paper, we design a SemCom system for a distributed multi-view scenario, where multiple semantic devices observe a scene and collaborate through a single semantic receiver to execute a task. We propose adopting an Over-the-Air Computation (AirComp) channel for efficient use of resources, as AirComp uses a superposition of signals to directly compute a function, which in SemCom is decoding the semantic variable. However, AirComp relies heavily on perfect time and phase synchronization, which is not practical in real-world communication. We show that timing offsets of standards like 5G cause negligible degradation, and that larger timing offsets can be compensated by training. Nevertheless, the system cannot deal with the encountered levels of phase synchronization errors, even when trained with those levels of synchronization errors. Therefore, we propose integrating existing phase synchronization algorithms into the AirComp SemCom system training. Simulation results show that the proposed system can approach the task execution performance of a perfectly synchronized SemCom system.
item.dc:creator: Maximilian H. V. Tillmann, Julian S\"undermann, Ahmad Halimi Razlighi, Edgar Beck, Armin Dekorsy

item.title: A Proof-of-Concept Study of Wi-Fi Channel State Information-Based Fall Detection Using ESP32 Devices
item.description: arXiv:2611.15532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper reports a small-scale proof-of-concept study of contactless fall detection using Wi-Fi channel state information (CSI) collected with two ESP32 devices. One device acts as the transmitter and the other as the receiver, with a separation of 3.5~m. The evaluated signal-processing pipeline uses CSI amplitude, second-level discrete wavelet transform (DWT) denoising with a Symlet-10 wavelet, z-score normalization, and fixed-length segmentation. Wavelet-scattering coefficients are used as features, and MATLAB's automated classifier-selection workflow identifies a LogitBoost ensemble with a minimum leaf size of four and a learning rate of 0.022052. The proposed classifier achieved an accuracy of 93.10%, with a precision of 100%, recall of 87.50%, and F1-score of 93.33%. These results demonstrate the potential of Wi-Fi CSI-based sensing for contactless fall detection using low-cost ESP32 hardware.
item.dc:creator: Amritha S. S., Anhajul S. Rahman, Mohammed Bin Saleem, Vaishnav Sankar, Jerrin Thomas Panachakel

item.title: Set-Theoretic PAPR Reduction in Multi-Antenna Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.15557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, we propose an optimization framework for PAPR reduction in multi-antenna systems with beamforming. Unlike previous techniques, the proposed approach permits full control over the distorted symbol constellation via arbitrary (convex) constraints on the frequency domain symbols, while minimizing the PAPR at each individual transmit antenna. We propose an iterative algorithm based on an extrapolated alternating projection method, which relies on an iterative soft-thresholding subroutine to compute projections onto sublevel sets of the objective function, and we compare its performance to optimal solutions obtained with general-purpose convex solvers.
item.dc:creator: Jochen Fink, Renato L. G. Cavalcante, S{\l}awomir Sta\'nczak

item.title: Physics-Informed Generative Augmentation for Open-Set UAV Classification
item.description: arXiv:2611.15612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-set recognition of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) from passive 5G radar micro-Doppler signatures is challenging because unknown drone types cannot be anticipated at training time. We propose a physics-informed generative adversarial network (PI-GAN) that conditions spectrogram synthesis on rotor kinematics, forcing the classifier's feature space to encode physically meaningful structure. We compare PI-GAN augmentation against a vanilla conditional GAN (CGAN) and basic data augmentation across three held-out configurations with 1, 2, and 3 unknown classes. Vanilla CGAN augmentation collapses open-set clustering, reducing the adjusted Rand index (ARI) from 0.97 to 0.01, whereas PI-GAN preserves it at 0.97. In a controlled held-out sweep with two unknown classes, PI-GAN achieves an ARI of 0.92 compared to 0.07 for vanilla CGAN. The physics-informed features enable unsupervised separation of mechanically distinct unknown drones without retraining, demonstrating that physics-conditioned generation is the key enabler of open-set capability.
item.dc:creator: Michel Kulhandjian, Levon Aslanyan

item.title: A Four-Branch Radar Target Simulator with Fractional Delay on a PlutoSDR
item.description: arXiv:2611.15674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Repeatable test setups support the development and evaluation of integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) hardware and algorithms. Commercial radar target simulators are expensive, while sub-6 GHz ISAC experiments often need only tens of megahertz of bandwidth within their available spectrum allocation. This makes simpler, low-cost test hardware attractive. We present a low-cost, open-source radar target simulator based on an ADALM-Pluto without hardware modification, supporting four independently configurable targets and analog bandwidths up to 56 MHz. The FPGA generates echoes with independent delays, Doppler shifts and gains, using fractional-delay filters for sub-sample adjustment. For motion-consistent echoes, delay and carrier phase are updated together to reproduce both changing range and frequency-dependent Doppler shifts. Over-the-air measurements demonstrate simultaneous echoes, sub-sample delay adjustment, and smooth target motion between sample positions. The FPGA source, firmware and on-device web interface are publicly available.
item.dc:creator: Florian Euchner, Stephan ten Brink

item.title: Reliable Near-Field Source Enumeration and Positioning Informed by Two-Stage MUSIC
item.description: arXiv:2611.15722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate and reliable near-field multi-source localization is essential for location-aware processing in future wireless systems. However, coherent multipath propagation complicates the direct recovery of line-of-sight (LoS) source positions, while existing estimation methods generally lack explicit control of the risk of source underestimation and positioning uncertainty. In this paper, we investigate reliable source enumeration and positioning in near-field coherent multipath environments. Specifically, we develop a conformal risk control (CRC) based source enumeration scheme that calibrates the penalty coefficient of an eigenvalue-based criterion to control the expected miss-detection ratio at a prescribed level. We further propose MUSIC-Net, a model-based deep learning framework informed by two-stage MUltiple SIgnal Classification (MUSIC), which learns the LoS-related subspace and surrogate distances through subspace-distance-based training, thereby enabling direct source positioning without estimating non-line-of-sight (NLoS) path parameters or performing subsequent path association. To quantify the uncertainty of the estimated positions, we develop a split conformal prediction (SCP) based calibration method that constructs angle-range predicted regions with finite-sample simultaneous coverage guarantees. Numerical results show that the proposed framework effectively controls the risk of source underestimation, while providing improved positioning accuracy with tighter predicted regions than benchmarks given the same target coverage levels.
item.dc:creator: Jiaying Li, Haifeng Wen, Changsheng You, Yuanwei Liu, Hong Xing

item.title: Rule-Sensitive Sensor Participation in Distributed Detection with Prescribed Boolean Fusion Rules
item.description: arXiv:2611.15824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study distributed binary detection when the fusion node must implement a prescribed Boolean decision rule. Under conditionally independent Bernoulli observations, we derive a signed-influence path identity valid for arbitrary Boolean rules; for monotone rules, it reduces to an exact Russo--Margulis representation in terms of coordinate influences. The identity yields rule-sensitive necessary conditions for a target Bayes error and an influence-weighted Kullback--Leibler feasibility bound. We then connect Boolean relevance to exact rule implementation and derive lower bounds on the number of sensors that must participate, including a heterogeneous bound based on the ordered per-sensor hypothesis separations. Numerical and Monte Carlo results illustrate both the tightening provided by the heterogeneous participation bound and the performance penalty that can arise when a prescribed fusion rule is retained instead of optimal likelihood-ratio fusion.
item.dc:creator: Ahmad Tanha

item.title: The BEATS Dataset: Towards Understanding Music-Physiology Dynamics in Real-World Scenarios
item.description: arXiv:2611.15837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the BEATS dataset, a robust compilation of psycho-physiological data collected in the wild from 30 participants while they listened to curated playlists intended to promote well-being. An acronym for Biomarkers, Experience and Affect from Therapeutic Soundscapes, the BEATS dataset aims to support research on wellbeing, music psychology, affective computing and signal processing. More specifically, this dataset includes: (1) sensor data collected during music listening sessions using a research-grade wearable device in free-movement environments; (2) music listening activity records, stimulus metadata, acoustic features, and self-reports associated with the listening sessions (3) individual characteristics, such as demographics, music preference, musical skills, and personality traits; and (4) self-reported psychological measures before and after their experimental participation spanning for a number of weeks. By situating data collection outside of lab settings, the BEATS dataset offers the opportunity to study real-world music-listening scenarios, allowing for a richer exploration of the physiological, subjective and therapeutic effects of music under real-world conditions.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Gutierrez Serafin, Tanaya Guha, Fahim Kawsar

item.title: NORA: Neuro-headstage for Online Recording and Actuation in Freely Behaving Animal Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.15936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents NORA, a compact wireless neuro-headstage designed for simultaneous neural recording and stimulation in freely behaving animal models. Separate recording and stimulation interfaces, each managed with a dedicated MCU and wireless module, are integrated into a fully head-mounted device compatible with standard Omnetics connectors; this separation allows for simultaneous recording and stimulation without sample-dropping or stimulation waveform distortion. To minimize stimulation artifacts and cross-domain interference, the recording and stimulation subsystems are electrically isolated with independent power domains and dedicated wireless communication paths. NORA has been validated through in vivo animal experiments, demonstrating acquisition of meaningful neural features with results comparable to a commercial wireless headstage. Together, these features establish a practical platform for artifact-reduced neuromodulation research.
item.dc:creator: Savanna Blade, Yuhan Hou, He Jia, Laura Kondrataviciute, Runtian Yang, Suneil K. Kalia, Xilin Liu

item.title: An Open-Architecture Dual-Core STM32-Based Neural Interface with Low-Latency On-Device AI for Neuromodulation Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.15942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an open-architecture bidirectional neural interface for closed-loop neuromodulation built around a dual-core STM32H747 microcontroller and commercial Intan recording and stimulation front-ends. The system supports up to 128 recording channels at 20 kSps and 64 stimulation channels while enabling low-latency on-device AI inference through a dual-core processing architecture and a two-stream memory hierarchy. To validate the machine learning pipeline, we demonstrate two neural decoding models, a compact multilayer perceptron executing entirely from on-chip memory and a larger temporal neural decoder utilizing external memory staging. Both models successfully decode fingertip velocity from neural spiking activity. As a proof of concept for closed-loop operation, we implement spike-triggered stimulation and achieve an end-to-end latency of $189 \pm 14\,\mu$s, representing an improvement of three orders of magnitude over a host-PC-mediated closed-loop pathway. These results demonstrate that resource-constrained embedded platforms can support high-channel-count neural interfacing, flexible on-device AI, and sub-millisecond closed-loop neuromodulation.
item.dc:creator: Sipeng Liang, Kun Cheng, Xiao Wu, Lyu Wang, Savanna Blade, Jiaxi Wei, Ruoheng Wang, Zhecheng Yin, Johnson Song, Tristan J. Lawson, Alisha Baldwin, Muhammad Shan Sohail, Luka Milosevic, Xilin Liu

item.title: Bilayer Periodically Poled Piezoelectric Thin-Film Lithium Tantalate Platform for Passive-Layer-Free Flexural and Torsional Actuation
item.description: arXiv:2611.16044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work demonstrates, to the best of our knowledge, the first passive-layer-free thin-film lithium tantalate (LT) actuator platform, supporting both out-of-plane flexural and in-plane torsional actuation from a single bilayer periodically poled piezoelectric film (P3F) X-cut LT stack. The polarity reversal across the bond interface flips the piezoelectric stress below the neutral axis, generating a bending moment without any passive elastic layer. Moreover, the two layers share identical elastic and thermal-expansion constants, making the stack thermally matched by construction. Suspended cantilever devices were fabricated on a single 2$\times$1.5 $\mu$m X-cut LT stack and verified by laser Doppler vibrometry (LDV). The tapered flexural resonator exhibits a 5.5$\times$ tip velocity amplification and a measured peak tip velocity of 10.3 m/s at $Q=634$, and a 0.49 MHz torsional cantilever resonator with $Q=514$ is demonstrated on the same stack. These results position bilayer P3F LT as a thermally matched, passive-layer-free actuation platform for vacuum-operated and optically interrogated MEMS such as scanners, gyroscopes, and ultrasonic transducers.
item.dc:creator: Tzu-Hsuan Hsu, Jiajun Huang, Zihuan Liu, Yen-Chen Wang, Vakhtang Chulukhadze, Neal Hall, Ruochen Lu

item.title: Real-Time Low-Complexity Zak-OTFS with Superimposed Spread Pilots on GPUs
item.description: arXiv:2611.16177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation offers robust performance under high-mobility scenarios. Spread pilots distribute pilot energy across the delay-Doppler grid and are superimposed with data symbols, enabling full-grid resource utilization. However, pilot-data separation challenges the design of the real-time receiver pipeline: cross-ambiguity in channel sensing incurs high computational complexity, and pilot-data interference cancellation requires repeated processing through turbo iterations. Leveraging the chirp structure of OTFS spread pilots, we reduce cross-ambiguity to a single 2D IFFT with element-wise chirp operations, achieving over 7000x speedup compared to partially vectorized direct evaluation on GPUs at a frame size of (M, N)=(2053, 31). Our real-time GPU baseband processing pipeline for OTFS with superimposed spread pilots supports (M, N)=(2053, 31) with one turbo iteration within a 1.03 ms latency budget. We further show that larger frames increase processing gain, allowing lower pilot power and near-converged bit error rate (BER) after one turbo iteration.
item.dc:creator: Chung-Hsuan Tung, Junyao Zheng, Vineetha Yogesh, Mudasir Ahmad Sheikh, Danish Nisar, Robert Calderbank, Tingjun Chen

item.title: Enabling Versatile Human Sensing through Wi-Fi Beamforming Feedback
item.description: arXiv:2611.16185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wi-Fi sensing enables contactless human sensing, while most existing systems rely on Channel State Information, which is accessible only on a limited range of Wi-Fi chipsets. In contrast, Beamforming Feedback Information (BFI) is standardized in modern Wi-Fi and readily accessible on a wide range of commodity devices, offering new opportunities for human sensing. In this paper, we present BeamLens, a Wi-Fi sensing system that extracts fine-grained spatial information from BFI to enable versatile human sensing. Specifically, we jointly estimate the angle of departure and relative time of flight from BFI to extract fine-grained spatial information and leverage two AP-STA links to capture complementary azimuth and elevation views. We further design a sparse physical antenna array and construct a uniform virtual antenna array to enhance spatial resolution. Moreover, we fuse complementary views through self-supervised learning, combining temporally aware cross-view contrastive learning and temporal masked reconstruction to learn a versatile backbone for diverse human sensing tasks. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that BeamLens achieves 90.16\% accuracy in human activity recognition, a mean per-joint position error of 8.64\,cm in 3D human pose estimation, and 70.64\% intersection over union in human silhouette estimation, while exhibiting strong generalization to unseen environments and subjects.
item.dc:creator: Jingzhe Zhang, Peiliang Wang, Yitong Shen, Ning Wang, Mingzhe Chen, Yili Ren

item.title: Cost of Decibel-Domain Averaging of Line-of-Sight States in Aerial Coverage Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.16288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) coverage studies routinely average the line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) path loss in the decibel domain, weighted by their probabilities. Since the conditional path-loss distribution is bimodal, the resulting mean path loss describes no physical link. We give the error of this mean path loss, relative to the path loss that corresponds to the mean received power, in closed form. We quantify it by ray tracing an ITU-R P.1410 city, supplying the averaged model with the exact LoS probability so that no parameter error contributes. Our numerical results show that the averaged path loss is 6.6 dB higher than the path loss of the mean received power and lies within 2 dB of only 6.2% of the links. It moves the coverage-optimal altitude from 1764 m to 778 m and understates the outage probability by up to 0.198.
item.dc:creator: Ismail Guvenc

item.title: A Theoretical Framework for Frequency-Shift Filtering-Based Interference Mitigation for OFDM Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.16292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) is widely adopted in modern wireless systems due to its high spectral efficiency and robustness to multipath propagation. However, its performance can be severely degraded by narrowband and wideband interference, particularly in spectrally congested environments where interference overlaps significantly in time and frequency with the desired signal. In this paper, we investigate interference mitigation for OFDM signals using the FREquency-SHift (FRESH) filter, which exploits cyclostationarity inherent to the waveform or induced by the modulation design. By leveraging correlations between frequency-shifted versions of the received signal, the FRESH filter provides optimal linear filtering for the cyclostationary processes. We first analyze the second-order statistics of OFDM signals with known structure and characterize their cyclostationary properties. Based on this analysis, we derive a compact closed-form matrix expression for the optimal FRESH filter coefficients under the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) criterion. The proposed framework enables offline computation of the filter coefficients when the signal structure is known and interference parameters are estimated, thereby reducing real-time implementation complexity. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in suppressing interference and improving detection performance compared to conventional approaches.
item.dc:creator: Xinrui Li, Karim Said, Daniel J. Jakubisin, R. Michael Buehrer, Jeffrey H. Reed

item.title: Physics-Aware Transformer-Based Beamforming Optimization for Near-Field E-MIMO ISAC Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.16305v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a physics-aware Transformer-based beamforming optimization (PATBO) framework for near-field extreme massive multiple-input multiple-output integrated sensing and communication (E-MIMO-ISAC) systems. PATBO combines regularized zero-forcing (RZF) communication directions and spherical-wave near-field sensing directions with learned stream-power allocation. A token-preserving Transformer maintains the correspondence between individual users/targets and their allocated powers, while a Cram\'er--Rao bound (CRB)-sensitivity-aware objective emphasizes power-allocation errors with greater localization impact. Physical feasibility is explicitly verified after inference, with infeasible predictions handled through physics-constrained power repair and optimizer fallback. For a $32\times32$ E-MIMO array with $1024$ antennas, the proposed structured representation reduces the learned output from $12{,}288$ real-valued coefficients of an unstructured complex beamformer to six stream-power variables. Direct PATBO achieves $100.98\%$ reference-rate retention and $19.54\%$ joint feasibility, which increases to $87.79\%$ after repair. The complete hybrid framework achieves $99.89\%$ reference-rate retention and $100\%$ constraint satisfaction on the retained test set, while requiring optimizer fallback for only $12.21\%$ of the scenarios. Direct PATBO inference requires $1.11$~ms per sample, corresponding to approximately $858\times$ and $779\times$ lower runtime than the evaluated cold-start and PATBO-warm-start sequential quadratic programming (SQP) implementations, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Mohsin Ali, Abdulahi Abiodun Badrudeen, Azharul Islam, Sunwoo Kim

item.title: Flexible Intelligent Metasurfaces for Enhancing Secure MISO Communications
item.description: arXiv:2611.16411v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This letter investigates flexible intelligent metasurface (FIM)-aided secure multiple-input single-output (MISO) communications in the presence of a multi-antenna eavesdropper. By exploiting the morphing capability of the FIM, the transmit array geometry can be dynamically reconfigured to reshape the legitimate and eavesdropping channels. We formulate a secrecy rate maximization (SRM) problem by jointly optimizing the transmit covariance matrix and the FIM surface shape. For a given FIM surface shape, the optimal transmit covariance matrix is shown to be rank one and is obtained in closed form from the dominant generalized eigenvector. For a fixed transmit covariance matrix, a projected gradient ascent (PGA) method is developed to optimize the FIM shape. Based on these two subproblems, a block coordinate ascent (BCA) algorithm is proposed. Moreover, for the special line-of-sight (LoS) scenario, we derive a globally optimal closed-form joint transmit covariance matrix and FIM surface shape design under a sufficient morphing-range condition. Numerical results demonstrate that FIM effectively improves the secrecy rate over a conventional rigid antenna array (RAA). Moreover, FIM achieves a transmit-power saving of about 2.5 dB compared with the RAA benchmark at the same secrecy rate.
item.dc:creator: Zihao Teng, Zihao Zhao, Jiancheng An, Lu Gan, Arumugam Nallanathan, Bo Ai

item.title: Synergizing Data-Driven Learning and Physical Rendering for Radio Map Prediction
item.description: arXiv:2611.16416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate urban radio map prediction is challenging due to complex building geometries and sophisticated electromagnetic interactions. To address this, we propose a data- and physics-driven framework that decouples wave propagation from environmental feature extraction. The core idea is to predict a sparse set of low-dimensional Secondary Reradiation Points (SRPs), which, together with a closed-form renderer deduced from electromagnetic theory, yields the final radio map. By learning these SRPs end-to-end rather than directly regressing the high-dimensional map, the neural network focuses on a compact physical parameterization, significantly improving accuracy and generalization. Numerical experiments demonstrate that our framework outperforms all seven baselines and consistently yields the lowest errors across all building-coverage quintiles, underscoring its robustness in dense, heavily obstructed urban environments.
item.dc:creator: Junyu Jiang, Jing Wang, Yantao Wang, Xinhao Li, Yi Zhang, Guangxu Zhu, Bin Wang

item.title: Delta-Iterations: A General-Purpose Linear Regression Solver for Huber's Penalty, $\epsilon$-Insensitive Loss, and Other Moreau Envelope-Based Loss Functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.16558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A general-purpose linear regression solver for a class of smooth loss functions is presented. The method applies to loss functions of the Moreau envelope type, which are continuously differentiable and have Lipschitz-continuous first derivatives. This class includes piecewise-defined cost functions consisting of constant, linear and quadratic segments, such as Huber's loss, insensitive least squares, one-sided least squares. The convergence guarantee provided by the associated proximal operator, the simplicity of the method and its versatility in handling various cost functions within a unified framework are its main advantages. MATLAB code for reproducing the numerical results presented in this article is provided.
item.dc:creator: Cagatay Candan

item.title: Certified Dynamic Subspace Optimization for Bayesian ISAC Design
item.description: arXiv:2611.16624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Full-space covariance optimization is costly in large-array Bayesian integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). A fixed transmit subspace can reduce this cost, but the resulting optimality loss depends on the posterior distribution. In this paper, a certified dynamic subspace method is developed for angle Bayesian Cram\'er-Rao bound (BCRB) minimization under joint angle and complex-gain uncertainty. For uniform linear arrays, exact response preservation over a nondegenerate posterior angular interval requires the full antenna space. Subspace sufficiency is therefore assessed through full-space objective-gap bounds. A communication-feasible basis is initialized from the user-channel span and local BCRB sensitivity. Restricted semidefinite programs are then solved. Primal restoration and dual repair yield gap bounds that remain valid after lossless user-beam recovery. When an accurate restricted solve does not certify the requested tolerance, the basis is expanded using a direction identified from the covariance dual slacks. Under a strict communication-power margin, joint uniqueness of the restricted optimal dual multipliers is established. With exact restricted solves, this uniqueness guarantees strict BCRB improvement after certificate-driven expansion. Numerical results validate the bounds against full-space references for the sampled problems. Compared with a fixed Fisher ordering, the proposed method can reach the same certificate target with fewer dimensions. On large arrays, total runtime is reduced relative to the full-space and factorized baselines at matched certificate targets.
item.dc:creator: Zongyao Zhao, Cheng-Jie Zhao, Zhaolin Wang, Qingjiang Shi, Yuanwei Liu

item.title: Empowering AI towards 6G: Realistic UAV Channel Data Acquisition using Open-Source Solutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.16644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The "sim-to-real" gap introduced by hardware impairments motivates realistic experimental platforms for AI-native research in Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN). This paper presents an open-source UAV-to-Ground measurement testbed built on the OpenAirInterface (OAI) stack and commodity Software Defined Radios (SDRs), enabling direct extraction of raw Sub-6 GHz Channel State Information (CSI) synchronized with flight telemetry. Through real-world flight campaigns, we observe a velocity-bandwidth decoupling effect: under unguided, measurement-only ridge extraction, dominant spectral ridges deviate strongly from the theoretical kinematic Doppler trajectory, whereas guided tracking substantially reduces this mismatch. This indicates that Doppler information is present, but not dominant, in the raw observable dynamics of commodity SDR-based measurements. We further benchmark representative deep learning predictors on this hardware-inclusive dataset and show, through a case study, that their behavior differs substantially from idealized expectations. By open-sourcing the testbed and dataset, we provide a realistic foundation for training and evaluating AI models for practical aerial network deployments.
item.dc:creator: Qiuheng Zhou, Sergiy Melnyk, Hans D. Schotten, Robert Vilter, Nick Stuckert

item.title: Measurement-Calibrated Synthetic Pretraining for Rapid Adaptation of UAV Channel Predictors
item.description: arXiv:2611.16646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) links can change faster than route-specific channel data can be collected, so a channel predictor must often be adapted from only a short target-flight calibration segment. This paper studies measurement-calibrated synthetic pretraining as an offline source prior for rapid adaptation of channel state information (CSI) predictors. The synthetic source is calibrated to flight-only power evolution, temporal shape variation, frequency selectivity, and phase disturbance, and is then combined with measured source-flight fine-tuning before target-flight adaptation. Under chronological held-out flight splits, synthetic-to-real (S2R) fine-tuning reduces the measured-data budget needed to reach useful prediction in the low-data regime. For 50 ms-ahead prediction, it crosses a latest-channel-estimate persistence baseline with 50 measured training windows, roughly 0.5 s of 10 ms-spaced supervised windows, whereas training from scratch requires 600 windows. A target-prefix adaptation study further shows that a lightweight gated recurrent unit predictor can reuse the pretrained source prior with one prediction-layer update epoch, positioning measurement-calibrated synthetic pretraining as a reusable prior for scarce target-flight measurements.
item.dc:creator: Qiuheng Zhou, Wei Jiang, Donglin Wang, Hans D. Schotten

item.title: Transferable Neuromorphic Protection for Distribution Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.16702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Protection of converter-dominated distribution networks is challenging due to limited fault currents, operating-mode transitions, bidirectional power flow, and heterogeneous network configurations. This paper proposes a scale-invariant neuromorphic protection framework to enable transferable protection decisions across such networks. The framework integrates asset-based normalization, multi-domain disturbance representation, event-driven spike encoding, leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) dynamics, adaptive threshold regulation, and directional supervision within a unified mathematical formulation. Local voltage, current, active power, and reactive power measurements are transformed into dimensionless disturbance representations, while latency encoding and membrane integration capture disturbance intensity and temporal evolution. The framework is evaluated across four heterogeneous network configurations: a two-DER inverter-interfaced microgrid, an islanded ring microgrid, the IEEE 13-node feeder, and the CIGRE European medium-voltage benchmark. Across 480 cases, it achieves a median operating time of 7.6 ms, with 94.2 % of cases operating within one power cycle. The results demonstrate selective protection across different electrical ratings and network topologies using a common parameterization without network-specific retuning, highlighting the potential of neuromorphic processing for physically interpretable, communication-free protection of converter-dominated distribution networks.
item.dc:creator: Saurabh Prabhakar, Yubo Song, Pascal Schirmer, Bijaya Ketan Panigrahi, Subham Sahoo

item.title: Directionally Supervised Neuromorphic Protection for Distribution Systems Using Local Measurements
item.description: arXiv:2611.16711v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reliable protection under varying power system operating conditions requires rapid fault detection while preserving selectivity against external faults and non-fault disturbances. This requirement is particularly challenging in communication-free schemes, where relays must determine trip conditions solely from local electrical measurements. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a directionally supervised neuromorphic protection scheme that integrates disturbance-responsive leaky integrate-and-fire dynamics with a direction-dependent firing threshold to distinguish internal faults from reverse-direction events. The unified relay architecture combines local disturbance detection, directional discrimination, and spike-based trip generation without requiring inter-relay communication. Its performance is evaluated under grid-connected and islanded conditions using a ring microgrid and the IEEE 13-node distribution feeder. Across 240 evaluated fault scenarios, the framework achieves median operating times of 5.4--7.6 ms across the two networks, with 78% of cases operating within 10 ms and 95% within 20 ms. It also maintains protection security during load disturbances, while fault-resistance analysis confirms its response under high-resistance faults. Controller-hardware-in-the-loop (CHIL) experiments using an RTDS simulator and an external dSPACE controller demonstrate trip-command assertion in approximately 10 ms and 5 ms for the tested single-line-to-ground and three-phase-to-ground faults, respectively. The results establish real-time feasibility within the evaluated conditions and characterize operating-time variability across fault types and resistance levels for different network configurations.
item.dc:creator: Saurabh Prabhakar, Yubo Song, Pascal Schirmer, Bijaya Ketan Panigrahi, Subham Sahoo

item.title: RadarML: A Multi-Channel Over-the-Air Dataset of Common Radar Waveforms for ES Evaluation
item.description: arXiv:2611.16786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces "RadarML", a publicly available dataset of modulated radar pulses recorded over-the-air across multiple semi-independent receiver channels. The dataset was generated using the UCL ARESTOR platform which is a Radio Frequency System on a Chip (RFSoC) based Software Defined Radio (SDR). The dataset contains a library of around two million waveforms with varying centre frequencies, bandwidths, pulse widths and modulations, with 1,000 examples of each signal variation per receiver channel. The goal of this dataset is to enable comparative analysis of radar modulation classification techniques on real data and stimulate research into multi-channel signal detection and modulation classification methods.
item.dc:creator: Ryan White, Adam Hosford, Matthew A. Ritchie

item.title: Asymptotic SINR Analysis of Linear Detectors in Uplink Massive NTN MIMO Transmissions
item.description: arXiv:2611.16851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper examines the performance degradation of receivers caused by imperfect channel state information (CSI), arising from training-based and semi-blind channel estimation techniques. We focus on the uplink of massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems operating in time-division duplexing (TDD) mode, considering the asymptotic regime where the number of base station (BS) antennas grows large while the number of users remains fixed. Leveraging random matrix theory (RMT), we analyze the asymptotic behavior of the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) under linear MRC and MMSE detection schemes. We derive closed-form approximations of the achievable rates, prove their asymptotic tightness, and validate their accuracy through simulations for systems of finite dimensions. Numerical results under realistic non-terrestrial network (NTN) conditions further demonstrate that semi-blind channel estimation enables MRC and MMSE receivers to outperform their training-based counterparts, while also quantifying the number of pilot symbols required to achieve a desired SINR level.
item.dc:creator: Xue Zhang, Abla Kammoun, Mohamed-Slim Alouini

item.title: Channel-Chart-Driven Antenna Activation for Energy-Efficient Cell-Free Massive MIMO
item.description: arXiv:2611.16996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) can provide uniformly high system performance across the coverage area through distributed cooperation. However, keeping all antennas active leads to high circuit and fronthaul power consumption. This paper studies energy-efficient uplink reception through antenna activation, where only a subset of distributed antennas is selected to serve the users. To enable network-wide activation with low signaling overhead, each access point (AP) maps its locally estimated channel state information (CSI) into a lowdimensional channel-chart (CC) embedding and forwards this representation to the central processing unit (CPU) instead of the full CSI. Based on the received embeddings, we formulate a binary antenna-activation problem for network EE maximization and propose three low-overhead strategies: (i) direct embeddingdomain activation using a proxy EE metric without CSI reconstruction, (ii) nearest chart-point CSI approximation, which estimates CSI from a reference chart database for greedy EE optimization, and (iii) decoder-based CSI reconstruction using a pre-trained autoencoder. The proposed approaches further enable a systematic comparison of antenna activation techniques in terms of achieved performance, computational complexity, and signaling overhead. Numerical results show substantial EE gains over the all-active baseline, with only a minor degradation in sum spectral efficiency and a significant reduction in signaling overhead. Moreover, the proposed greedy framework achieves EE performance close to that of the simulated annealing baseline, confirming its effectiveness for low-complexity antenna activation.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: WiMob 2026 - The 22nd International Conference on Wireless and Mobile Computing, Networking and Communications., Oct 2026, Avignon (FR), France
item.dc:creator: Yara Kafa (INSA Rennes), Luc Le Magoarou (INSA Rennes, IETR), Joumana Farah (INSA Rennes, IETR), Matthieu Crussi{\`e}re (INSA Rennes, IETR)

item.title: EEGDash Corpus: A Training-Ready Public Corpus for EEG Foundation Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.06356v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models are pretrained on tens of thousands of hours. The largest clinical archives restrict redistribution, while public datasets use different formats and licences. Here, we rebuild the 77 redistributable datasets of the REVE pretraining corpus that reach its 200 Hz input (14,075 hours across 7,272 subjects) and release them as eegdash-corpus-v0, with raw-file access by name through EEGDash and a checksummed Zarr store on Hugging Face, converted with REVE's preprocessing recipe. Every dataset keeps its licence, and any subset of datasets can be selected by name. To test whether this public store pretrains REVE-Base, we train the model twice from scratch with REVE's trainer and score it on seven public OpenEEGBench tasks. First, under linear probing, the frozen encoder reaches 0.331 in chance-adjusted balanced accuracy, against 0.333 for the released model (untrained: 0.200), a difference smaller than the spread between our two pretraining seeds. Second, after fine-tuning, it reaches 0.273 against 0.325 published (0.301 in our rerun), and part of this gap comes from the scoring pipeline. A public, training-ready EEG corpus can therefore pretrain the frozen representations of a foundation model and provide a shared base that other groups can audit.
item.dc:creator: Kuber Shahi, Bruno Aristimunha, Arnaud Delorme

item.title: Multi-Step Underwater Acoustic Channel Prediction via Dual-Domain Structure Preservation and Pretrained Transformer
item.description: arXiv:2611.14592v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate future channel state information (CSI) is essential for underwater acoustic (UWA) communication because delays associated with signal propagation, feedback, scheduling, and transceiver reconfiguration can render currently available CSI outdated. However, most existing predictors estimate only the next channel state and obtain multi-step forecasts through recursive rollout, which causes prediction errors to accumulate as the multipath structure evolves. The scarcity of sea-trial measurements further limits reliable model training. To address these challenges, we propose LLM4UACP, a dual-domain, structure-preserving framework that adapts a pretrained Transformer for few-shot multi-step UWA channel prediction. LLM4UACP extracts complementary features from the channel impulse response (CIR) and channel frequency response (CFR), aligns them through Fourier-consistent fusion, and encodes the fused representation as delay-time tokens. A pretrained Transformer with a frozen backbone is adapted through Butterfly Orthogonal Fine-tuning to jointly predict multiple future CIRs in a single forward pass, thereby avoiding the error accumulation associated with recursive prediction. Experiments on the measured SO-06 and SO-07 channels show that LLM4UACP achieves normalized mean squared error (NMSE) values of 0.0411 and 0.0399, corresponding to reductions of 88.53% and 85.15%, respectively, relative to the most recent baseline. With only 0.11M trainable parameters, LLM4UACP maintains robust performance across varying prediction horizons and observation-window lengths, limited-data settings, and cross-dataset transfer scenarios.
item.dc:creator: Mingjie Cao, Gewei Zhang, Deqing Wang, Lizhao You, Fei-Yun Wu, Liqun Fu

item.title: Risk-Aware Joint Inference and Resource Control for Physical AI in 6G Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.14696v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Wireless edge inference enables Physical-AI devices to execute edge-inferred actions using transmitted sensory inputs. Since the risk of incorrect actions vary across observations and tasks, the associated uplink transmission of sensory inputs requires different levels of wireless reliability. For instance, applying a fixed signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) requirement can overprovision low-risk tasks while underprovisioning high-risk ones. Therefore, we propose risk-aware control for edge inference (RACE), which maps predicted action-failure probability and task criticality to adaptive SINR targets and combines them with deadline-derived SINR requirements. A slow-timescale large language model (LLM) proposes task requirements for deterministic validation, while a fast hybrid actor selects inference configurations and transmit power levels, complemented by analytical receive beamforming and finite power restoration. Simulations show $11\%$ improvement in the average accuracy-latency-energy objective over fixed-high-SINR control, with near-zero constraint outage.
item.dc:creator: Amin Farajzadeh, Melike Erol-Kantarci

item.title: Reduced-Complexity WMMSE Approach for Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems With Finite-Capacity Fronthaul Links
item.description: arXiv:2611.15054v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a reduced-complexity weighted minimum mean squared error (R-WMMSE) framework for cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) systems with finite-capacity fronthaul links. To maximize the system capacity, we need to jointly design beamforming vectors at distributed access points (APs) and fronthaul quantization noise covariances. Such a task would be addressed using conventional WMMSE algorithms and their variants. However, existing WMMSE-based methods either assume ideal infinite-capacity fronthaul links or incur high computational complexity when jointly optimizing the network-wide beamforming and fronthaul compression variables. To this end, the proposed method jointly optimizes beamforming and fronthaul compression by leveraging a sequential per-AP optimization strategy. Since each subproblem is efficiently solved via Lagrangian duality with closed-form updates, the overall computational complexity can be significantly reduced compared to the conventional WMMSE method. To further reduce hardware cost, we extend the R-WMMSE framework to hybrid analog-digital beamforming systems, tackling the joint design of digital beamforming, fronthaul compression, and analog beamforming. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme achieves performance nearly identical to that of the conventional WMMSE while reducing the runtime by over 99%.
item.dc:creator: Wonsik Yoo, Hoon Lee, Seok-Hwan Park

item.title: A Diffusive T-Matrix Unifying the Electric and Magnetic Polarizability Tensors in Conducting Layered Media
item.description: arXiv:2611.15090v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Electromagnetic induction is used to detect and classify buried and submerged objects, such as unexploded ordnance in soil and on the seabed. A small object is commonly described by its magnetic polarizability tensor (MPT), which is independent of its position and of the sensor. The MPT assumes that the surrounding medium does not conduct. In seawater at extremely low frequency, or in clay at kilohertz frequencies, this assumption fails at depths comparable to the skin depth. The object then also diverts the current induced in the medium, a galvanic response that the MPT omits. We describe the object instead by its transition matrix (T-matrix), which keeps the independence from position and sensor and includes both responses. It is computed once per medium and frequency from a single finite element problem, for any shape and materials. Its inductive block reduces to the MPT when the medium conducts weakly, and its galvanic block reduces to the electric polarizability tensor in the static limit. We test the model against full finite element solutions for a conducting box, non-magnetic and permeable, in a layered sea and in clay over bedrock. Two orders beyond the dipole, it is accurate to within 1.4% over two decades of frequency and for sizes up to 0.7 of the depth, whereas the error of the MPT carried into the conducting medium reaches 91%. Blocks coupling the two responses, contained in neither tensor, contribute up to 13%.
item.dc:creator: Fraser Williams, Dhammika Jayalath, Clinton Fookes, Ajay Pandey

item.title: Multimodal Semantic Communication using Shared and Unique Representation Decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2611.15357v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) has emerged as a promising paradigm for bandwidth-constrained mobile and vehicular networks. This paper proposes a unified representation learning framework for multimodal SemCom (MSC), which encodes heterogeneous data into a compact semantic space for efficient transmission and source recovery. The framework addresses the multimodal semantic representation gap, which arises when at least one modality contains semantic information that cannot be fully inferred from the other. To preserve this information for reconstruction, the framework decomposes each representation into shared and modality-specific components. We formulate a mutual information objective for source reconstruction, cross-modal alignment of the shared components, and decoupling of the shared and modality-specific components. To enhance transmission efficiency, we introduce a shared knowledge base implemented as a compact codebook of semantic vectors learned during training. The shared components are transmitted digitally as codebook indices, while the modality-specific components are sent in analog form. We apply knowledge distillation during training, using a pretrained vision foundation model to guide the learning of quantized shared features. On image--text pairs over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and Extended Vehicular A (EVA) channels, the proposed framework improves image reconstruction over conventional separate source-channel coding (SSCC) and representative multimodal and unimodal SemCom systems. Further evaluations show gradual degradation under channel-estimation mismatch, complementary effects of alignment, decoupling, and knowledge distillation on the shared representation, and alignment of shared features across modalities with separation of the modality-specific features.
item.dc:creator: Peng Yi, Ying-Chang Liang

item.title: VR-Net: Subarray-Level Inter-Cell Coordination for Multi-Cell XL-MIMO under Near-Field Spatial Non-Stationarity
item.description: arXiv:2611.15393v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spatial non-stationarity in multi-cell extremely large-scale MIMO (XL-MIMO) confines each user to a visibility region (VR) of each array. VR-Net exploits these regions for subarray-level coordinated beamforming. A base-station (BS)-indexed conflict graph identifies overlapping VRs; gain-based association and a masked multi-cell weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) iteration restrict beam design and channel state information (CSI) uploads to the relevant subarray blocks. We establish conditions for exact per-cell decoupling, derive the expected CSI loads, bound the loss of designing on the VR-gated channel and the loss of the support constraint, and characterize single-edge visibility contrast through a closed-form Fresnel transition width. Simulations use a 3GPP TR 38.901 Release-19-based near-field UMi channel with modular facade arrays and pre-registered criteria. At a 30 dB threshold, VR-Net retains at least 99.6% of the full-aperture WMMSE sum rate in every tested setting while uploading 10-39% fewer complex CSI entries. It gains up to 3.5 bit/s/Hz over an all-user adaptation of the multi-cell scheme of P\'erez-Ad\'an et al. at moderate power and dense load, and inter-cell coordination adds up to 33% over per-cell design.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Shoaib Ayub, Rana Muhammad Subhan, Insoo Koo, Felipe Augusto Pereira de Figueiredo

item.title: Optimization of Finite Alphabet Message Passing Decoding on Fully Node-Parallel Architectures for 5G LDPC Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.15694v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel design method for the lookup tables (LUTs) of the minimum reconstruction, computation, and quantization (min-RCQ) LDPC code decoding algorithm. The proposed design method uses Bayesian optimization and samples from a subspace of the design space. The novel design method does not require knowledge about the channel or the modulation format and uses the frame error rate (FER) as loss function. The design method is applicable to irregular low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes with puncturing and shortening. Furthermore, the design method creates a set of iteration-agnostic LUTs that can be used over all iterations, which makes this approach suitable for fully node-parallel decoder architectures. We show that our proposed approach achieves a 38.6 % better energy efficiency than a state-of-the-art normalized min-sum (NMS) decoder without loss in error correction performance.
item.dc:creator: Alexander von Bank, Oliver Griebel, Eike-Manuel Edelmann, Norbert Wehn, Laurent Schmalen

item.title: Learning Mixtures of Exponential Family
item.description: arXiv:2611.15698v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by causal inference and physical computing systems, we consider the problem of learning mixture of two bounded-support exponential-family distributions with a shared interaction parameter matrix and mixture component-specific linear parameter vectors. The unknown sequence of component labels belongs to a known structured class. We propose an estimator based on a convex loss that avoids the log-partition function; for each fixed label assignment, estimation is a convex optimization problem. We show that the conditional population loss uniquely identifies the interaction matrix and the linear parameter attached to each sample. For a global empirical minimizer, we establish finite-sample bounds on the interaction error in Frobenius norm and the average squared linear-parameter error. The bounds depend on the logarithm of the number of admissible label assignments, and, for fixed dimension and model bounds, imply consistency when this complexity grows sublinearly with sample size. Additional occupancy and separation conditions yield component and label recovery.
item.dc:creator: Mansi Sood, Devavrat Shah

item.title: Privacy-Preserving Spectrum Data Obfuscation in Next-Generation Spectrum Coexistence Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.15770v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In spectrum coexistence systems, the primary user (PU) activity must be partially disclosed for interference avoidance and coordination, while the exact spectrum occupancy information is often restricted due to security and regulatory constraints. To this end, subset-based disclosures can be employed in which the true frequency is included while ambiguity is introduced. This paper shows that naive randomized subset disclosures remain highly vulnerable to information leakage through inference, as temporal structure can be exploited to recover spectrum usage information. Under Markovian dynamics of the PU's spectrum usage, hidden Markov model (HMM) filtering with online learning is applied, while under periodic dynamics, period and phase estimations with phase-aligned statistics are used for inference. To address this vulnerability, structure-aware obfuscation strategies are introduced. For Markovian dynamics, history-based and belief-based schemes are designed to induce model mismatch and limit posterior concentration, while for periodic dynamics, cycle-dominance and decoy-based schemes are designed to manipulate phase-wise statistics and bias the inference process. These obfuscation schemes significantly hinder inference of spectrum information and offer principled disclosure solutions for spectrum coexistence systems.
item.dc:creator: Yalin E. Sagduyu, Tugba Erpek, Sastry Kompella, Joseph A. Molnar

item.title: Subject-Held-Out Evaluation of Deep Ground Reaction Force Estimators Across Two Laboratories: Leakage and Cross-Laboratory Transfer
item.description: arXiv:2611.15966v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep networks that estimate ground reaction forces and centers of pressure from motion-capture markers are validated within one laboratory, in a seldom-stated coordinate frame, and sometimes with trial-level splits that put the same person in the training and the test set. We measured what each practice costs, and whether such models transfer between laboratories. Three sequence models (convolutional, convolutional-recurrent, and convolutional-transformer) were evaluated on two independent datasets, locomotion (6 subjects) and occupational patient handling (10 subjects), under one pipeline, one tuning procedure, three seeds, and four protocols: trial-level split, leave-one-subject-out, pooled two-laboratory training with matched held-out subjects, and cross-laboratory transfer. At a fixed configuration, trial-level splits overstated the subject-held-out coefficient of determination by +0.040 to +0.194; on occupational data the overstatement exceeded every difference between architectures. With subjects held out, the three models reached values between 0.583 and 0.804; the leader differed between datasets, and gaps lay within subject-to-subject variability. Pooling the laboratories changed neither dataset on matched subjects. Transfer between laboratories was below chance in both directions, including the vertical force, which no in-plane rotation can affect. Leaving force targets in the plate frame while inputs were heading-aligned cost 0.57 of locomotion anteroposterior-force explained variance, enough to make that force look hardest; a Newton's-law correlation detected the mismatch before training. Split protocol and target frame changed reported accuracy more than architecture did. Learned force estimators should be validated with subjects held out, checked for frame consistency before training, and tested across laboratories before deployment claims are made.
item.dc:creator: Hernan David Santos, Yinong Chen, Yu Ding, Xudong Zhang, Jian Tao

item.title: An $O(L^3)$ Spherical Harmonic Transform on $L^2$ Samples
item.description: arXiv:2611.16441v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the representation of signals on the sphere band-limited at $L$ using the optimal number of samples, $L^2$, equal to the number of degrees of freedom in harmonic space and placed on $L$ iso-latitude rings, we develop a spherical harmonic transform (SHT) that is theoretically exact, requires no solution of linear systems and no precomputation beyond the placement of the rings, and has complexity $O(L^3)$. The transform rests on the observation that, for each order $m$, the samples on the rings that resolve order $m$ are a complete set of samples for the order-$m$ profile of the signal, so that its values on the remaining rings follow from a closed-form Lagrange basis, the sampling functions of order $m$. We prove that the proposed optimal-dimensionality SHT (OSHT) recovers every band-limited signal exactly in exact arithmetic, so that the $L^2$ samples admit a sampling theorem in the collocation sense. For the final harmonic analysis we give two exact back-ends: Gauss-Legendre quadrature of the interpolated profiles and the algorithm of the equiangular sampling theorem, which applies without change because the rings coincide with its grid. We identify the amplification constant that governs numerical error, show that it replaces the condition number used previously for the placement of rings, propose a placement that minimizes it, and give an error propagation model that explains the growth of error with the band-limit. A multi-pass refinement converges in two passes to the rounding floor of the samples. We also describe a stable log-domain evaluation of the sampling functions, a rescaled Legendre recurrence, and a forbidden-region skipping rule that halves the cost of the elimination. Numerical experiments up to $L=2048$ characterize the accuracy, measured by the maximum and mean coefficient errors and the signal-to-noise ratio, the stability and the computation time.
item.dc:creator: Zubair Khalid

item.title: Context-Predictive Low-Rank Adaptation for Face Presentation Attack Detection
item.description: arXiv:2611.16534v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Face presentation attack detection requires representations that distinguish physical spoofing cues across changes in acquisition devices, subjects, and attack media. Large visual encoders offer transferable representations, but conventional binary fine-tuning supervises their final decisions without explicitly constraining how local facial evidence is represented under partial observation. We present CP-JEPA, a context-predictive adaptation framework that combines low-rank tuning of a pretrained CLIP image encoder with a joint-embedding predictive objective. A student predicts complete-image teacher features at masked spatial locations, while unmasked classification, masked classification, and prediction consistency retain the connection to the live/spoof task. An exponential-moving-average teacher supplies evolving latent targets. The auxiliary components are used only during training; inference requires only the LoRA-adapted CLIP visual encoder and binary classifier. {We evaluate CP-JEPA under single-source and multi-source OCIM transfer, additional CelebA-Spoof training, transfer to CelebA-Spoof, two-source training, and unseen-attack evaluation on SiW-Mv2.} On the standard OCIM benchmark, CP-JEPA achieves 3.74\% mean HTER and 98.73\% mean AUC. {Single-source evaluation achieves 11.36\% mean HTER across twelve source--target combinations.} With CelebA-Spoof added to the three OCIM training sources, CP-JEPA reduces mean HTER from 3.45\% to 2.35\% and increases mean AUC from 98.68\% to 99.32\%. On SiW-Mv2, it achieves 3.36\% mean HTER across the held-out attack categories. Controlled loss ablations examine the contributions of latent prediction, masked classification, and prediction consistency. The results show that context-predictive adaptation can improve cross-dataset PAD performance, although the gains vary with the training sources and evaluation setting.
